t: Domain Model Generator - Signature build-tool concept
title: Domain Model Generator - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Represents important real-world concepts and their relationships.
description:
Domain Model Generator is the Signature build-tool concept that represents important real-world concepts and their relationships. In the Signature line, it is not a loose collection of scripts but a deterministic capability: the same build request produces the same verified result on every run, on every machine. This database documents the concept in full - what it is, the seven framework pillars that implement it, the real techniques it stands on, the standards it honors, and laddered drills that teach it from first principles to compounded mastery.

An AI that builds on demand needs Domain Model Generator the way a workshop needs its central bench. Without it, every build becomes improvisation: requirements drift, steps run out of order, and nobody can say why a result came out the way it did. With it, the build becomes a protocol - inputs declared, transformations explicit, outputs checked against the original request. That protocol is what these records describe, pillar by pillar.

Every record in this database carries a runnable demonstration program, because a build tool that cannot show its work cannot be trusted with real work. Read the overview, study the pillars, practice the drills, and run the demos: by the end the Domain Model Generator will be a capability you can invoke, not a concept you have read about.

t: Signature Cartographer - Domain Model Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Cartographer - Domain Model Generator framework pillar
definition: The Cartographer component of the Signature Domain Model Generator framework, owning cartographer. Signature concept.
description:
The Cartographer is a load-bearing component of the Signature Domain Model Generator framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's cartographer responsibilities belongs to the Cartographer, and the Cartographer answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Cartographer can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Cartographer works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Domain Model Generator charter (represents important real-world concepts and their relationships.). The Cartographer reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for an small architecture job that needs Domain Model Generator. The Cartographer takes the request's cartographer responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Cartographer's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Domain Model Generator. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Contractor - Domain Model Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Contractor - Domain Model Generator framework pillar
definition: The Contractor component of the Signature Domain Model Generator framework, owning contractor. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Domain Model Generator framework, the Contractor owns the framework's contractor responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Contractor's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Contractor from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Represents important real-world concepts and their relationships.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Software architecture and system design build needs Domain Model Generator, so the framework invokes the Contractor on the the framework's contractor responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

t: Signature Stratifier - Domain Model Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Stratifier - Domain Model Generator framework pillar
definition: The Stratifier component of the Signature Domain Model Generator framework, owning stratifier. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Domain Model Generator framework decomposes the capability (Represents important real-world concepts and their relationships.) into seven pillars, and the Stratifier is the one that owns the framework's stratifier responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Domain Model Generator result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Stratifier's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Stratifier's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.
